scope.summary: Hydrate the HBR matrix for all BodyKit MTs per Section 13.27: INT/SWARM/VIS/QUIET/MAN/STOP rows populated for MT-478..653 with evidence references (swarm proof MT-607, Argus matrices MT-634/645, manual MT-651), gaps recorded as typed deferrals — and hbr-matrix-check green.
acceptance_criteria: Every BodyKit MT (478..653) has hydrated HBR rows across INT/SWARM/VIS/QUIET/MAN/STOP with a posture and an evidence reference or a typed deferral reason — no blank cells.
VIS rows reference the persisted Argus capture matrices (MT-634 GUI, MT-645 QA bodies); SWARM rows reference the MT-607 concurrency proof; MAN rows reference the MT-651 chapter entries.
QUIET rows confirm headless BodyKit runs pop no foreground windows and steal no focus (evidence from the headless test runs).
hbr-matrix-check runs green over the hydrated matrix; the check is wired into the packet's validation flow so future MT additions without HBR rows fail fast.
Deferred tiers (internal_diagnostics, Palmistry per WP-KERNEL-012/016) carry the standard deferral reasons consistently across all rows.
scope.risk_if_missed: BodyKit ships with untracked harness-behavior obligations — no auditable answer to 'is this surface swarm-safe, quiet, manual-covered' — and the packet fails its own HBR directive at integration validation.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
